record.title: Latent Sparse Attention reports long-context attention speedups up to 10M tokens
record.summary: A preprint introduces Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries search cluster summaries rather than score every key. In author-run tests, its distilled form stayed near the tested model baselines at contexts up to 10M tokens and reduced attention-layer prefill and decode time substantially on two specific model families and H200/B300 hardware. The paper reports smaller end-to-end serving gains than the per-layer headline; its 100M-token result is an extrapolation. The linked implementation could not be accessed during this review, and no independent reproduction was performed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors posted arXiv:2610.42147v1 on 2026-10-30 describing Latent Sparse Attention, with a distilled variant for pretrained models and a native-training variant.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In their tests, the authors report that D-LSA on GLM-5.3-Flash retained similar measured accuracy through 10M-token contexts and reduced one attention layer's prefill and decode time by 22.7x and 4.6x versus the model's sparse-attention baseline. On Qwen-3.8-27B they report 72.4x and 42.5x versus full attention at 10M tokens. End-to-end time-to-first-token gains were 2.2x and 9.2x, respectively. These results use author-selected hardware, benchmark settings and model configurations.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent replication, comparable gains across other model families or serving workloads, broad economic savings, or measured accuracy and speed at 100M tokens; that scale is extrapolated. The linked code repository returned 404 when checked.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent implementation or reproduction of the reported accuracy and performance results was inspected; the paper-linked GitHub path returned 404.
Generalization beyond the two tested model families, single-request production-serving measurements and H200/B300 setups is unestablished; the 100M-token prefill curve is extrapolated.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains hold beyond the tested setups, reducing attention indexing costs at multi-million-token contexts could change inference-system design for multiple frontier-model teams. The paper tests to 10M tokens, but does not establish generality or independent reproduction.
limitations: All reported performance and accuracy measurements are from the authors; no independent reproduction was performed.
The linked public code path returned 404 during review despite the paper describing the code as released.
Per-layer speedups are not end-to-end speedups; reported end-to-end time-to-first-token gains are 2.2x and 9.2x.
The end-to-end serving timing uses one request at a time and the median of three requests of 256 output tokens.
The measured long-context evaluation reaches 10M tokens. The 100M-token tree-search result is extrapolated, and the paper leaves native training at larger scale and longer contexts open.
brief.summary: A preprint introduces Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries search cluster summaries rather than score every key. In author-run tests, its distilled form stayed near the tested model baselines at contexts up to 10M tokens and reduced attention-layer prefill and decode time substantially on two specific model families and H200/B300 hardware. The paper reports smaller end-to-end serving gains than the per-layer headline; its 100M-token result is an extrapolation. The linked implementation could not be accessed during this review, and no independent reproduction was performed.

technical.claimed_result: At 10M tokens, the paper reports one-layer speedups of 22.7x prefill and 4.6x decode for GLM-5.3-Flash against its sparse-attention baseline, and 72.4x/42.5x for Qwen-3.8-27B against full attention. End-to-end time-to-first-token gains are 2.2x and 9.2x, respectively. Accuracy is described as similar to the corresponding model baselines in the tested benchmarks.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports H200 and B300 measurements, one-request-at-a-time end-to-end serving with three 256-output-token requests, and 10M-token contexts. It does not establish deployment-wide cost or economic savings.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors published a 43-page preprint with benchmark and timing details. These are author-reported measurements; the code repository URL cited in the paper returned 404 at review time and no reproduction was run.
technical.mechanism: LSA groups keys into clusters in a learned latent space. Queries score cluster summaries and select long-range keys rather than scoring each key. D-LSA distills projections into pretrained models; N-LSA trains natively using next-token prediction. Tree search is the paper's subquadratic variant.
technical.regime: Author-reported evaluations of D-LSA on Qwen-3.8-27B with full-attention baseline and GLM-5.3-Flash with sparse-attention baseline, contexts up to 10M tokens, H200 and B300 accelerators, and SGLang serving. N-LSA training results are at 128k context on a roughly 0.5B-parameter model.
technical.strongest_baseline: For GLM-5.3-Flash the comparison is its existing sparse-attention implementation; for Qwen-3.8-27B it is full attention. These are different baselines and the speedup figures should not be compared as one matched contest.

brief.title: Latent Sparse Attention reports long-context attention speedups up to 10M tokens
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported quality and serving gains generalize, reducing the indexing cost of sparse attention could make very long model contexts more practical for long-horizon agent and scientific workflows. The evidence is bounded to author-run evaluations on two model families, a small request setting and specified accelerators; it does not establish broad deployment economics or reliable performance beyond 10M tokens.
